packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET packet-04 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind first reading)

EXPOSURE STATEMENT
Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification, author, work or earlier
reading of this item. The only extraneous information visible is in the images
themselves: ownership stamps reading "BIBL. UNIV. GENT" (ink) and
"BIBLIOTHECA GANDAVENSIS" (blind stamp). I have not tried to identify the work.

====================================================================
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)
====================================================================
Observations
- Two overviews: image-001 (face A) and image-014 (face B). Each shows an opened
  bifolium of paper (laid lines visible), landscape, with a central fold. Each
  half carries two narrow columns, so four columns per face. A cm scale lies
  under the sheet; the sheet is roughly 33 cm wide by about 21 cm high.
- Column lengths are unequal and the lower third of the sheet is blank on both
  faces, apart from a three-line addition written across the foot of the left
  half of face A.
- Small, very rapid, heavily abbreviated cursive in brown ink, one hand
  throughout as far as I can tell. No running titles, no rubrication, no
  coloured or enlarged initials. Section breaks are marked only by short blank
  gaps, double virgules (//) and a slightly larger opening letter.
- Many lines are underlined with thin horizontal strokes (face A cols 2, 3, 4
  especially; face B cols 2, 3). Whether this is emphasis, ruling or a
  cancellation convention I cannot tell; on face B col 3 one line looks
  genuinely struck through with a heavier stroke.
- Marginal labels beside the columns: face B has "[p]a 2o //" (read as
  "prima conclusio"), a second similar label lower in the gutter between cols 1
  and 2, "tia 2o" ("tertia conclusio") at the foot of col 1 and again at the
  foot of col 2, and "No //" (nota?) near the top. Face A has "3a / ..." in the
  gutter between cols 3 and 4 and two faint marginal words left of col 3 near
  its foot.
- Face A, foot of left half: three long lines linked by drawn braces/arrows at
  both ends, apparently an addition to be inserted into the column text above.
- Damage: large irregular holes and skinned/abraded patches around the central
  fold in the lower half of both faces; a row of small sewing/stab holes along
  the foot; small worm-like holes. In the skinned areas grey offset of printed
  black-letter type shows vertically (the leaf was evidently in contact with or
  pasted to printed matter), and reversed show-through of the other face is
  visible.
- Face B col 1 has a blank gap after two opening lines, then a new section
  beginning "Utrum ...".

Tentative interpretations (not observations)
- The text reads as continuous scholastic prose organised as questions with
  numbered arguments and numbered "conclusiones", not as lemma plus gloss. I
  saw no separate commentary layer or interlinear gloss.
- Column order within each face is assumed left to right. I could not establish
  the order of the two halves of the bifolium or which face precedes; the text
  does not obviously run on from the foot of one column to the top of the next
  in every case (see limitations).
- Face A col 2 lower part is set out in short lines that may be a list or
  diagram-like division rather than prose; much of it is lost.

====================================================================
2. SPANS SELECTED / LEFT UNREAD
====================================================================
Selected: face A col 1 (whole, with foot addition), col 2 upper half, col 3 upper
two thirds, col 4 upper two thirds; face B col 1 (question opening and foot),
col 2 top, col 3 top, col 4 (whole).
Left largely unread: face A col 2 lower half and col 3/col 4 lowest lines
(holes, abrasion, print offset); face B col 2 and col 3 middle and lower parts
(skinned surface, holes); face B col 1 lines 10-14 of the section (faint).

Conventions: ( ) = my expansion of an abbreviation; ? after a word = uncertain
reading of that word; [..] = letters I could not read; [illegible] = unreadable
stretch; / and // = virgules written by the scribe. Line numbers are counted
from the top of the named tile and include partly cropped lines; they are
approximate to within one line where the tile begins mid-line.
This hand is extremely cursive. Expansions of common abbreviations (q(uod),
(con)-, -(ur), diffi(niti)o, demo(nstrati)o) are fairly secure; individual
words marked ? are not.

====================================================================
3. FACE A (overview image-001)
====================================================================

--- Face A, column 1 (image-002, continued in image-006 and image-010) ---

5. LIMITATIONS
====================================================================
- The hand is a very fast, heavily abbreviated cursive. Function words and the
  recurring technical terms are reasonably secure; many content words carry a
  question mark and several lines in each column are only partly read. The
  proper names in face A col 1 and the possible name in face B col 3
  (image-021 L4) are especially uncertain.
- The top line of face A cols 3 and 4 and of face B col 3 is cropped by the
  sheet edge or tile edge (descenders only), so the leaf appears trimmed at
  the head or the text continues from elsewhere.
- Lower halves of face A cols 2-3 and face B cols 2-3 are lost or skinned
  around the central fold; printed black-letter offset and reversed
  show-through overlie what remains. These gaps are a property of the leaf.
- Gaps in face A col 4 lines L12-L16 and image-009/013, and in face B col 1
  image-019 L10-L15, are partly a property of my reading of faint ink rather
  than of loss; a higher-contrast or raking-light image would help.
- Column order within a face, the order of the two halves of the bifolium, and
  which face comes first are not established. Face A col 1 clearly continues
  into the foot addition; face A col 3 to col 4 and face B col 3 to col 4 seem
  to run on in subject but I could not confirm a verbal join.
- The pervasive thin underlining was not treated as deletion; only strokes
  through the letter-bodies were reported as deletions (image-003 L10,
  image-010 L8, image-021 L11, image-025 L5).
- Suggested further views: a contrast-enhanced crop of face A col 2 lower half
  and of the foot addition; an enhanced crop of face B col 1 middle
  (image-019 L9-L15); and the heads of all columns with the sheet edge included.
